chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd Al-Ajaly, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who blinded an eye of a Christian. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The wergild (blood money) of the eye of a Christian is four hundred dirhams.'

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or financial compensation for injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for blinding a Christian's eye according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the diyah (blood money) for injuring the eye of a Christian (Nasrani) at 400 dirhams, illustrating the Shia jurisprudential principle of varying compensation based on the victim's religious status. It reflects the historical context of the Dhimmi contract, where non-Muslims residing under Muslim rule received specific financial protections distinct from those afforded to Muslims. This ruling is foundational in understanding the application of 'udl (compensation) in Shia fiqh regarding inter-faith injuries.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Bureyd Al Ajaly who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a Muslim man who blinded an eye of a Christian. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wergild of an eye of a Christian is four hundred Dirhams’.
